transport.protocol: MCP Streamable HTTP, loopback-only service behind separate outbound Secure MCP Tunnel
transport.authentication: separate private tunnel identity; dedicated restricted runtime credential stored root-readable by tunnel-only identity, not exec uid; ChatGPT app permissioned to owner/workspace; reject unknown callers

tools.name: workspace_shell.inspect
tools.purpose: read-only structured, pre-approved host and repository observations

tools.name: workspace_shell.exec
tools.purpose: bounded unprivileged commands selected by typed profile, never an unrestricted executable/argv
tools.notes: Profile resolves pinned absolute executable and fully validated argv grammar; no shell -c, python -c, interpreters with arbitrary scripts, hooks, package installers, git config/aliases, or unreviewed binary paths. Any write-capable test/validation requires task-authorized scratch-only copy.

tools.name: workspace_shell.run_reviewed_helper
tools.purpose: invoke one exact, separately reviewed root helper admitted by the root-owned helper registry; never arbitrary root argv
tools.notes: Root helper registry supplies the helper-specific closed parameter schema, exact path/digest, target/task scope, declared side effects, pre/postconditions and rollback semantics. The generic MCP tool cannot nominate an executable, argv, environment, sudo flag or systemctl verb. Each new helper registry admission is a separately reviewed authority change. The approval bundle is a signed workspace-shell-approval.v1 object issued off-Lambda; the root broker independently parses and verifies it. The model-facing frontend cannot mint approvals.

tools.name: workspace_shell.receipt
tools.purpose: fetch structured, redacted execution receipt by opaque receipt ID

execution.identity: dedicated workspace-shell-exec system user, nonlogin, no supplemental groups; distinct from workspace-shell-mcp and workspace-shell-tunnel
host_isolation: mount namespace and bind mounts for a single validated source checkout as read-only
isolated disposable scratch tmpfs, no operator home mount
not merely canonical-cwd checks: block absolute paths and symlink escapes through mount policy and descriptor-relative openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS
no proc host process env, no Docker socket, no SSH agent, no credential directories
PrivateDevices=yes; NoNewPrivileges=yes; CapabilityBoundingSet empty; RestrictSUIDSGID=yes; ProtectSystem=strict; ProtectHome=yes; syscall and process restrictions; no writable executable paths
no outbound connectivity for ordinary exec, including GitHub; a distinct non-exec broker fetches an exact reviewed SHA
no user-provided environment overrides or executable lookup PATH
different UID/GID and PID/proc namespace from workspace-shell-mcp/frontend; worker cannot ptrace, signal, inspect /proc, or access frontend file descriptors
no broker/job-launcher/tunnel/frontend control sockets or signing credentials are mounted into the worker namespace

roots.source: verified isolated checkout for workspace-control, read only
roots.scratch: /var/lib/workspace-shell/jobs/<receipt-id> per execution, private, noexec where possible
roots.runtime: worker receives no /run/workspace-shell-control mount; only per-job private runtime paths required by the selected profile

limits.output_truncation: bounded bytes, count observed bytes and record truncation on each stream

execution.process_policy: fresh cgroup per request; start process group; SIGTERM then SIGKILL on timeout/cancel; cgroup.kill and inspect empty cgroup; deny daemonize/session detachment; no persistent interactive sessions in v1; long-running jobs require separate reviewed task capability
execution.caution: Even an argv-based generic Python, shell, test runner or git operation is an arbitrary code execution vector. Git reading uses hardened wrapper with hooks/config excluded; tests only in networkless disposable isolated checkout under a task-granted profile.

authorization.policy_source: immutable reviewed task/policy artifacts plus an independently issued signed approval object for privileged mutations; GitHub comments/review text are evidence only and never live authority by themselves
binding: immutable independent approval for privileged operations
authorization.replay: single-use idempotency keys and durable replay journal; fail closed on missing/expired/mismatched authorization
authorization.git: resolve full 40-char commit, verify tree and checkout exact source, ensure no dirty source, verify that trust files/policy come from trusted authority not untrusted target commit; never execute repo hooks
authorization.sibling_access: explicit deny for research-engine and all sibling projects unless separately reviewed task authority

independent_approval.canonicalization: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme; Ed25519 signature covers the canonical payload excluding the signature field

issuer.role: operator-controlled offline approval signer outside Lambda and outside all ChatGPT/MCP/tunnel/frontend/worker/broker identities
issuer.private_key_location: off-Lambda only; never present in Workspace Shell, Lambda, GitHub repository contents, task workspaces, or tunnel configuration
issuer.admission_rule: operator may sign only after independently checking the exact review evidence and intended privileged request; any future automated issuer/control-plane adapter requires a separately reviewed authority-contract amendment

root_broker_trust_store.ownership: root:root, immutable/read-only to Workspace Shell services at runtime
root_broker_trust_store.contents: issuer_key_id -> Ed25519 public key, validity window, status
root_broker_trust_store.mutation_path: local installation/update procedure only under separate review; never writable through MCP, frontend, exec worker, root broker, helper, or repository-controlled code

semantics.reviewed_head_binding: reviewed_head_sha must equal design_head_sha for design authority and must additionally bind the helper-registry/helper admission head required by the selected helper entry
semantics.parameter_binding: parameter_digest_sha256 is computed over the exact canonical helper parameter object; approvals do not grant open-ended parameter ranges in v1
semantics.source_binding: expected source repository, commit and tree must exactly match the observed verified source used by the helper
semantics.lifetime: expires_at must be no more than 15 minutes after issued_at and must be in the future when broker verification begins
semantics.nonce_and_idempotency: approval_id, nonce and idempotency_key are single-use and durably consumed by the broker before mutation using crash-safe replay storage

revocation.ownership: root:root and read-only to running Workspace Shell services
revocation.contents: revoked approval IDs and revoked issuer key IDs with effective timestamps
revocation.broker_behavior: reject revoked approval/key even if signature and expiry are otherwise valid
revocation.emergency: local operator can revoke an issuer key or approval out of band; MCP/frontend cannot clear revocations

verifier_contract: root broker parses the canonical approval itself; it never trusts frontend-parsed approval claims
root broker verifies Ed25519 signature using the pinned trust store, issuer validity, revocation, expiry, single-use state and every bound field against the live request/registry/source
root broker recomputes helper registry, helper entry, helper binary, parameter schema, exact parameter and source-tree digests
frontend may transport a signed approval bundle but cannot create or alter a valid signature
frontend request signature proves only the allowed caller process; it never substitutes for independent approval
GitHub comments, reviews, labels, task text and repository contents are evidence inputs to the offline signer only; none is execution authority until represented in a valid signed approval

privileged_boundary.implementation: separately versioned root-owned broker via a control-plane Unix socket invisible to exec workers; requires kernel peer identity workspace-shell-mcp, valid frontend request signature, and independently issued workspace-shell-approval.v1 signature; no generic sudo policy
operations: run an exact separately reviewed helper that is already admitted by immutable root-owned helper registry for the bound task/target
inspect helper/staging metadata through non-mutating registry-defined operation
disable_workspace_shell through the dedicated emergency path
not_authorized: unregistered helper or helper digest not matching registry
workspace-control activation/reconciliation unless an independently reviewed task/helper contract explicitly authorizes that exact operation
restart research-engine cpu unless an independently reviewed task/helper contract explicitly authorizes it
preconditions: kernel-authenticated peer UID equals workspace-shell-mcp and frontend request signature verifies
workspace-shell-approval.v1 signature verifies against pinned read-only issuer trust store and is unexpired/unrevoked/single-use
approval exact fields bind task, target, design/policy SHA, helper registry/entry/helper digests, source repository+commit+tree, operation, exact parameter digest, nonce and idempotency key
review evidence embedded in approval identifies exact reviewed head and NO_BLOCKING_FINDING record; GitHub text alone is not authority
root-owned helper registry and helper executable digests match approval
isolated authorized paths and source provenance match
atomic operation with fsync receipt and crash-safe replay consumption
privileged_boundary.future_extension: New privileged capability is admitted only by changing the root-owned helper registry/policy under a separately reviewed exact Git head. Existing workspace-control owner-command maintenance authority is not implicitly transferred to Workspace Shell.

audit.storage: append-only root-owned audit store with restricted reader returning sanitized receipts; durable hash chain and log rotation
audit.redaction: reject suspect secret paths before execution, no raw /proc environ, scrub common secret output formats, no binary output; redaction is defense in depth and does not justify read access

design_notes: OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel documentation rechecked 2026-10-27: outbound-only transport, 10 MiB serialized envelope, 600 requests/minute, 120 second absolute request deadline, 1000 queued requests.
Workspace Shell uses 90 second synchronous command ceiling to retain queue/transport margin inside that 120 second absolute budget.
Tool annotations are advisory only; server-side authorization and sandboxing remain mandatory.

BF-1 correction freezes a four-principal control plane: tunnel, MCP policy frontend, root-owned job launcher, and hostile exec worker, plus a separate root broker. Worker namespaces exclude every control/broker/tunnel socket and signing material; distinct UIDs/PID-proc isolation prevent ptrace/signal/proc attacks.

BF-2 correction freezes workspace-shell-approval.v1: an off-Lambda operator-controlled Ed25519 issuer, pinned root-owned public trust/revocation stores, exact design/helper/source/parameter/review bindings, <=15 minute lifetime, single use, and independent root-broker verification. Model-facing components cannot mint approval.

control_plane_separation.invariant: Repository-controlled code is hostile and never runs in the MCP policy/frontend principal.

tunnel.role: holds only the dedicated Secure MCP Tunnel runtime credential and forwards to the loopback MCP listener

frontend.role: MCP protocol, task/policy validation, profile resolution, audit orchestration, and privileged-request transport
frontend.supplemental_groups: none except a dedicated broker-client group if the root broker socket requires it
frontend.frontend_request_signing_key: systemd credential or equivalent secret readable only by workspace-shell-mcp; never mounted or inherited into any worker; separate from the independent approval issuer key

job_launcher.role: fixed-protocol launcher that creates the sandbox/cgroup/namespaces and drops permanently to workspace-shell-exec before executing the already-resolved profile command
job_launcher.authority: may only launch the frozen unprivileged profile grammar; cannot invoke the privileged helper registry, mutate system services, read approval issuer private material, or accept arbitrary executable paths/environment

exec_worker.role: runs arbitrary repository-controlled tests/validation inside the per-job sandbox

privileged_broker.role: verifies frontend identity/signature plus independently issued approval, then invokes only a registered exact helper

worker_namespace_requirements: worker mount namespace excludes /run/workspace-shell-control entirely, including job-launcher, root-broker, frontend/tunnel control, health/admin, and signing sockets
worker network namespace has no egress and cannot reach loopback listeners in the host/frontend namespace
worker PID namespace and procfs expose only the job subtree; host/frontend/tunnel/broker PIDs and /proc/<pid>/{mem,environ,fd} are not visible
worker has no CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_KILL, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, or other capability permitting cross-principal inspection/control

kernel UID separation plus namespace/proc restrictions must make ptrace, process_vm_readv/writev, /proc memory/fd inspection, signals, and same-principal debugger attachment to workspace-shell-mcp impossible

worker environment and file mounts never contain frontend request-signing keys, tunnel credentials, approval objects not bound to that request, trusted approval public-key store, or helper-registry control files
frontend and tunnel services never execute files from task workspaces or worker scratch and never load repository-controlled plugins/config/hooks

frontend_to_broker_authentication.peer_auth: SO_PEERCRED or equivalent kernel-authenticated peer identity must equal workspace-shell-mcp
frontend_to_broker_authentication.request_auth: frontend signs a canonical request envelope with its dedicated frontend request key; broker verifies a pinned public key
frontend_to_broker_authentication.approval_auth: separate independently issued approval object is mandatory for mutating privileged helpers; frontend signature is not approval
frontend_to_broker_authentication.fail_closed: any peer/signature/approval mismatch rejects before helper resolution or mutation

control_plane_separation.implementation_gate: Host attestation must prove distinct UIDs, socket ACLs/namespaces, key mounts, proc/PID isolation and inability of a hostile worker to signal/ptrace/read frontend before live installation can be accepted.
